issue.title: Update: Nodejs_Security_Cheat_Sheet
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?

The Node.js Security Cheat Sheet is about 5,500 words with 271 lines of code, and nearly all of it sits under one "Recommendations" heading.

- "Use flat Promise chains" is about 115 lines, 94 of them code. That is code-quality advice, not a security control.
- Many topics restate other cheat sheets (CSRF, logging, security headers) instead of linking them.
- The brute-force section is already being reworked in #2775.

## How should this be resolved?

- Break "Recommendations" into a few real sections so the sheet is easy to scan.
- Drop or cut down advice that isn't a security control, starting with the Promise chains section.
- Cut code to the smallest example that shows the point, and link to package and Node.js docs for the rest.
- Where a topic has its own cheat sheet (CSRF, Logging, HTTP Headers), keep only what is Node-specific and link out.
- Coordinate with #2775 so the brute-force rework and this cleanup don't collide.

Small PRs, one section at a time, please. They are much easier to review than one big rewrite :)

2890.title: docs: update Node.js CSRF protection guidance (#2797)
2890.body:
### Description

Updates the `Use Anti-CSRF tokens` subsection in the Node.js Security Cheat Sheet with focused, Node.js-specific CSRF protection guidance.

The change recommends using framework-provided CSRF protection where available, clarifies token validation for state-changing requests, and explains that `SameSite` cookies provide defense-in-depth rather than standalone protection. It also removes outdated guidance around the deprecated `csurf` package and links to the dedicated OWASP CSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet.

The change is limited to this subsection. All surrounding guidance remains unchanged, including the brute-force section being handled separately under issue [[#2775](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/issues/2775)](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/issues/2775).
